MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING
  JUNE 20, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 6:00 p.m. at Ernie Howlett Park, 25851 Hawthorne Boulevard,
  Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR CIAROLLA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CIAROLLA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, Ciarolla, Persichina, Pope, Romanelli,
  McCormick, and Retz (joined at 6:05 pm)

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF MAY 16,
  2022

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  MAY 16, 2022.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
JUNE 20, 2022
   A.  PICKLEBALL PROGRAMMING

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the proposed
  pickleball programming.

  COMMISSIONER POPE inquired about the target audience and recommended
  adding information regarding age ranges to the programming flyer.

  B.  RENEWAL OF TENNIS SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI inquired about the class rates and past class price
  increases in comparison to current increase. ACM Davis responded that class rates
  in the area were taken into consideration, and that Tennis Pro, Mr. Krueger felt the
  increase was reasonable was not a concern.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if Mr. Krueger commented on his future
  plans with regards to the tennis club. ACM Davis responded that while Mr. Krueger
  did not offer details regarding his future plans, he indicated that he was very
  comfortable with the term of the five-year agreement.

  COMMISSIONER POPE inquired about the reason Mr. Krueger was interested in
  separating Tracy Austin Doubles Tournament Director task from the agreement.
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that Mr. Krueger expressed
  interest in stepping away from the to allow a new director to step in, to potentially
  enhance the tournament as we continue to modernize the coordination of the
  tournament. Supervisor Pinuelas added the Mr. Krueger also offered to help in a
  different capacity or even stay on as director if needed, as he did not want to
  negatively impact the tournament.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  POPE to:

  RECOMMEND THE CITY COUNCIL ENTER INTO THE PROPOSED FIVE-
  YEAR TENNIS SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH TENNIS PRO ROBERT
  KRUEGER TO CONTINUE TO PROVIDE TENNIS PROGRAM SERVICES
  AT THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES TENNIS CLUB.

  AYES: Pope, Romanelli, Retz, Persichina, McCormick, Bain, Ciarolla
  ABSENT: None

  The motion carried.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
JUNE 20, 2022
   C.  PUBLIC RIDING RULES UPDATE

  Assistant City Manager Davis gave a brief overview of the staff report.

  ACM Davis stated that staff is looking to permanently effectuate the temporary
  modifications to no longer limit training hours on weekends and holidays at
  Chandler Arena by revised resolution as well as clarify the currently posted limit of
  two horses per trainer with a maximum of six horses in the arena to permit
  recreation rider access by resolution in response to COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA regarding the number of horses.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA stated that there have been instances where there are two
  trainers with two students each and all are on their horses. She stated this is an
  issue for recreational riders because Chandler Arena is not large enough to
  accommodate more than six horses.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by CHAIR CIAROLLA to:

  RECOMMEND THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE AN UPDATE TO THE
  CITY’S PUBLIC RIDING RING RULES AS PROPOSED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  D.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK PERIMETER PATHWAY PROJECT UPDATE

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the staff report
  and ACM Davis provided an engineering update on the project status.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if the Pagliano family is aware of the dedication and
  naming of the pathway. ACM Davis noted that the dedication of the pathway and
  placement of the plaque in honor of Dr. Pagliano took place after it was approved
  by Council in 2012 and the plaque is placed at the entrance to the bridle path, but
  staff will connect with the family about the updated work being done.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  ACM Davis provided information regarding an upcoming Interpretive Design
  meeting being held by the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy and Acorn
  on Friday and invited Commissioners, requesting no more than three due to Brown
  Act limitations. No Commissioners indicated availability.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
JUNE 20, 2022
   A. ADOPT-A-PARK

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted overgrown areas on the George F
  Canyon trail.

  B. MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A. CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MAY 10, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B. CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MAY 24, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI suggested adding a future agenda item to address
  unpermitted sports field use with informational signage.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided information regarding an
  unauthorized use of the baseball field for a travel ball summer camp program
  involving a local travel ball team and Silver Spur Little League. Supervisor Pinuelas
  also pointed out current signage posted regarding sports field use.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained the court usage options for
  Pickleball in response to COMMISSIONER POPE. ACM Davis pointed to the new
  signage posted identifying the pickleball courts.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas and Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith provided information regarding proposed Spur Little League
  improvements that had been reviewed by the Youth Sports Subcommittee,
  including a temporary scoreboard, the newly replaced permanent scoreboard,
  temporary extension of fencing facing the bridle trail and the possible turf
  replacement of the infields.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted improvements to the barn stalls and
  identified sloped areas in response to COMMISSIONER BAIN.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
JUNE 20, 2022
   Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith identified areas that would be improved as
  part of the Perimeter Pathway Project.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CIAROLLA MOVED TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:25 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON JULY 18, 2022, AT
  6:00 P.M., WHICH BE HELD AT HIGHRIDGE PARK, 29035 HIGHRIDGE
  ROAD, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90275.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Rosa Pinuelas  Valerie Ciarolla
  Community Services Supervisor  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
JUNE 20, 2022
